title: You’ve heard what culture says about marriage.
paragraphs:
You’ve heard what culture says about marriage.
“Follow your heart.”
“Do what makes you happy.”
“Leave when it gets hard.”
But that’s not what God said.
And deep down… you already know the difference.
Because you’ve seen what happens when love is built on feelings alone. It fades. It fractures. It turns into something unrecognizable. God saw it. You knew.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

God didn’t create marriage just to make you happy.
He created it to reveal something eternal.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
In the beginning, before there were weddings, rings, or vows, there was intention. In Genesis, God said:
“Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.” (Genesis 2:24)
Read that again.
One flesh.

Not two individuals coexisting.
Not a contract you can walk away from.
One.

That means what you do affects them.
What you say cuts deeper.
What you hide… breaks something sacred.
Marriage, in God’s eyes, is not casual. It is covenant.
And covenant is not built on convenience.
Then comes the part most people avoid.
Because it confronts you.
In Ephesians, God speaks directly to husbands:
“Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave Himself up for her.” (Ephesians 5:25)

Not “when she respects you.”
Not “when she deserves it.”
As Christ loved.
How did Christ love?

He sacrificed.
He endured rejection.
He bled.
He died.
That’s the standard.
And suddenly, love isn’t just emotion anymore… it’s death to self.

You said you love her.
But do you die to your pride for her?
Do you lay down your anger, your ego, your selfishness?
God saw it.
You knew.
And then He turns to the wife.
“Wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands as you do to the Lord.” (Ephesians 5:22)
This is where resistance rises.
Because the world twisted that word into oppression.
But biblical submission is not about inferiority. It’s about divine order. It’s about trust in God’s design.

It’s choosing respect even when emotions scream otherwise.
It’s choosing honor in a world that celebrates rebellion.
And no—this does not excuse abuse, control, or sin. God never blesses what violates His character.
But it does expose something deeper:
You don’t struggle with submission because of your spouse.
You struggle because surrender is hard.

To him.
And to God.
Now here’s where everything shifts.
Because marriage is not ultimately about you.
In Ephesians 5:31–32, it says:
“This mystery is profound, and I am saying that it refers to Christ and the church.”
Marriage is a mirror.
A living, breathing picture of Jesus and His people.

The husband reflects Christ’s sacrificial love.
The wife reflects the church’s devotion and trust.
So when marriage breaks…

It’s not just a relationship falling apart.
It’s a reflection being distorted.
That’s why the enemy attacks it so aggressively.
Because if he can destroy marriage, he can blur the image of Christ.
And maybe that’s where this hits you.
Because if you’re honest…

You haven’t loved like Christ.
You haven’t respected like the church.
You’ve held onto bitterness.
You’ve justified silence, distance, even betrayal.
God saw it.
You knew.
And this is the tension.

Because God’s standard is high.
Higher than what you can achieve on your own.
So what now?
This is where the Gospel steps in.
Because the same Jesus who calls you to love and submit…
Is the same Jesus who died for your failure to do it.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
You didn’t meet the standard.
He did.
And then He took your place.

Your pride.
Your anger.
Your selfishness.
Your broken view of love.
All nailed to the cross.
So marriage isn’t just about trying harder.
It’s about being transformed.

When Christ changes you…
You begin to love differently.
You begin to forgive faster.
You begin to choose humility over being right.
Not perfectly.
But genuinely.
And now the question isn’t “Is my spouse worth it?”
The real question is:
Is Jesus Lord over your marriage… or are you?

Because one leads to restoration.
The other leads to slow destruction.
And you can already see which direction you're heading.
If you felt that conviction… that’s not random.
That’s God knocking.
Say it plainly if it’s real:
“I need God to fix what I broke.”
Type it. Mean it.
There’s more depth waiting—real teaching, real correction, real growth. If you’re ready to stop playing with your faith and start walking in it, step into it here:
This isn’t just content.
This is a turning point.
